children: Apple
has entered its first new CEO era in 15 years, with longtime hardware chief
John Ternus replacing Tim Cook on September 1

. Cook's farewell memo closed one of corporate America's most successful leadership runs, but investors are already looking beyond the handoff toward Ternus's bigger challenge: keeping Apple's hardware machine growing while accelerating its response to the AI boom.
Cook leaves behind a dramatically larger Apple. During his tenure, annual revenue nearly quadrupled to more than
$416 billion
, while the company's market capitalization climbed from roughly
$350 billion to $4.6 trillion
, according to the supplied report.
The truth is, whatever there is to say about my success, I know it is all because of you, Cook told employees in his final memo. You have brought out the best in me.

Ternus brings deep product experience after more than two decades at Apple, most recently leading hardware engineering across products including the iPhone, Mac and iPad. Cook will remain deeply involved as executive chairman, providing continuity as Ternus takes responsibility for Apple's broader strategy.
The transition comes with Apple's underlying business in strong shape. Fiscal third-quarter revenue rose
16% to $109.4 billion
, while diluted EPS jumped
. Apple also posted June-quarter records for iPhone, Mac and Services revenue, giving Ternus a strong financial base as he takes over.
The harder question is innovation. Apple continues to face pressure to demonstrate that it can compete more aggressively in AI while maintaining its dominance in premium consumer hardware.
Investors Takeaway
Ternus gets his first major public test almost immediately. Apple's
September 9 Surprise and Shine event
is expected to feature the next iPhone lineup and potentially the company's first foldable iPhone, which could open a higher-priced new category and help stimulate upgrades.
Investors should watch
iPhone demand, Services growth, gross margins and adoption of Apple's newer AI features

. The September event will matter, but the larger test is whether Ternus can translate his hardware background into a broader innovation cycle strong enough to preserve the extraordinary growth and valuation Apple built under Cook.

title: Apple Turns to John Ternus for Its Next Chapter
